evidence: Receiving DO2 at t=52.0h: 10.95 mg/L (online sensor), well above the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving DO2 trajectory shows the mid-run dip to ~8.4–9.1 mg/L during t≈24–28 h with recovery to ~12–12.6 mg/L after t=28 h, consistent with scheduled aeration/operation
Receiving delayed P assay: 0.0 g/L at 12h/24h, 1.08 g/L at 36h, 3.07 g/L at 48h — active production phase with no mass loss
All three source batches show the same DO2 pattern and comparable P trajectory, indicating the receiving vessel is performing within established envelope
No DO2 excursion below constraint; retain product mass favors no feed cut or stop
args.rationale: The receiving fermentation is following the well-characterized source-batch envelope: a normal mid-run DO2 dip to ~8.4 mg/L near t=24-28h (mirrored in all three source batches), which recovers after the aeration step; DO2 at decision time (52h) is ~10.9-11.5 mg/L, far above the 2.0 mg/L oxygen floor. Product assays show healthy production onset at 24-28h and P=3.07 g/L at 48h, consistent with sources (~3.0 g/L at 48h). No oxygen-constraint risk, no product-mass concern, and no anomalous divergence between receiving and source trajectories. Feed reductions (reduce_feed, strong_feed_reduction) would slow production; increase_air is unnecessary since DO2 is ample. This is a normal case requiring no intervention.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters/states are unknown; DO2 could decline faster in the remaining run if metabolic demand rises, but current levels (~11 mg/L) leave a large margin above the 2.0 mg/L constraint, and the source batches reached end-of-run DO2 around 7.4-9.1 mg/L without intervention. Residual risk that late-run oxygen demand exceeds aeration capacity is low but not zero; an extra assay was not needed given consistent online-sensor evidence across four batches.
